items.definition:
a person or country that attacks first
The aggressor nation launched an unprovoked attack.

a precious stone of a clear purple or bluish violet color
Her necklace had a beautiful amethyst pendant.

a system of reading and writing for the blind
Books in braille allow visually impaired people to read.

a device for launching objects
The ancient army used a catapult to hurl stones at the castle walls.

a tooth on the rim of a wheel or gear
Each cog in the machine plays a vital role.

an aromatic spice
Add a teaspoon of cumin to the chili for extra flavor.

a design prepared on special paper for transfer onto another surface
She put a decorative decal on her laptop cover.

a print made from an engraved plate
The museum displayed an old engraving of the city skyline.

eucalyptus
The koala was eating eucalyptus leaves.

exhibitor
The exhibitor showcased their new product at the trade show.

expatriate
Many expats live in Dubai for work.

ferret
A ferret is a small, domesticated mammal.

goosebump
The cold air gave me goosebumps.

a state of inactivity and metabolic depression in endotherms
Bears go into hibernation during the winter.

a Hawaiian dance
She learned to dance the hula on her trip to Hawaii.

the process of making a person or animal immune to infection
Childhood immunization is crucial for public health.

the state of being inaccurate
There were several inaccuracies in the report.

the area of a baseball field enclosed by the bases
The shortstop made a great play in the infield.

Japanese characters derived from Chinese characters
Learning kanji is a big challenge for Japanese learners.

a particular language or jargon
I don't understand all the technical lingo.

a married woman, especially a dignified or elderly one
The head nurse was a stern but fair matron.

a type of dumpling native to Tibet and Nepal
We ordered a plate of delicious momos for lunch.

a quantity of food or drink that fills the mouth
He took a big mouthful of pie.

unit of electrical resistance
The resistance of the circuit was measured in ohms.

a mythical monstrous humanoid creature
In fantasy stories, orcs are often depicted as green-skinned and brutish.

a player in baseball who plays in the outfield
The center fielder made an amazing catch.

a flow outwards
There was a significant outflow of capital from the country.

an introduction to something more substantial
The orchestra began with an overture before the main opera.

a disease characterized by skin eruptions
Chickenpox is a common childhood illness.

an attempt to make something that is not the case appear true
He made a pretense of being busy, but he was actually doing nothing.

a member of a group of English Protestants of the late 16th and 17th centuries who regarded the Reformation of the Church of England under Elizabeth I as incomplete and sought to simplify and regulate forms of worship
The Puritans sailed to America seeking religious freedom.

a disorderly crowd; a mob
The speaker tried to calm the angry rabble.

one of several internal beams extending from the eaves to the ridge of a roof, supporting the roof covering
The old barn had exposed wooden rafters.

the controlled distribution of scarce resources, goods, or services
During the war, there was strict rationing of food and fuel.

a person who redeems someone or something
Many Christians believe in Jesus Christ as their Redeemer.

a new issue or version of a previously released item
The band announced a special reissue of their classic album.

an electrical component that resists the flow of current
A resistor is used to limit the current in an electronic circuit.

A mixture of fat and flour used as a base for sauces
First, make a roux with butter and flour for the cheese sauce.

A letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
The ancient stone was carved with mysterious runes.

A greeting, especially in Arabic-speaking countries
He greeted his friend with a warm 'salam'.

A person who can see the future
The ancient seer predicted a time of great change.

Fair and generous behavior or treatment of others, especially in a sports contest
Good sportsmanship is essential in any competition.

A group of lines forming the basic recurring metrical unit in a poem or verse
The poem consisted of three stanzas.

A person who deals or trades in something illegal
The police arrested a suspected drug trafficker.

umpire (informal)
The batter argued with the ump about the call.

a small, hard, benign growth on the skin
He had a small wart on his finger.

a large hairy creature said to live in the Himalayas
Some people believe in the existence of the yeti.

a person appointed to a position
The new appointee will start next month.

the quality of being difficult to use or deal with
There was an awkwardness in the silence between them.

an officer of the court
The bailiff called the next case.

an obstruction in a pipe or channel
There was a blockage in the drain.

an anchored float serving as a navigation mark
The boat was tied to a buoy in the harbor.

a person who campaigns for a cause
She is a passionate campaigner for environmental protection.

a piece cut or trimmed from something
She saved the newspaper clipping about the event.

an award or official praise
He received a commendation for his bravery.

the scientific study of crime
She decided to major in criminology at university.

a Russian emperor
The last czar of Russia was Nicholas II.

the process of providing electricity
The electrification of rural areas improved living standards.

the end of a period of time
Check the expiry date on the milk carton.

the quality of being loyal or true
Her faithfulness to her friends was unwavering.

the thigh bone
The femur is the longest bone in the human body.

a person who works for themselves
He works as a freelance writer.

a clear, tasteless protein obtained from animal products, used in food preparation
The dessert was made with fruit and gelatin.

a machine with a heavy blade sliding vertically in grooves, used for beheading people
The guillotine was a symbol of the French Revolution.
